name: Build an LED Circuit
description: Build a simple LED circuit on a breadboard with a resistor and battery.

steps.instruction: Place the LED on the breadboard. Insert the longer leg (positive/anode) into hole E10 and the shorter leg (negative/cathode) into hole E11.
steps.visual_cue: The LED should be straddling the center gap of the breadboard with legs in column E.
common_errors: LED legs in the same row
LED inserted backwards (short leg in E10)

steps.instruction: Take the 220 ohm resistor — it has red, red, brown, and gold colored bands. Insert one leg into hole A10 and the other leg into hole A6.
steps.visual_cue: The resistor should bridge from row 10 to row 6, connecting to the same row as the LED's positive leg.
common_errors: Resistor not in the same row as LED anode

steps.instruction: Take a red jumper wire. Connect one end to hole A6 (same row as one end of the resistor) and the other end to the positive (+) power rail on the side of the breadboard.
steps.visual_cue: Red wire goes from row 6 to the red (+) rail.
common_errors: Connected to wrong rail (negative instead of positive)

steps.instruction: Take a black jumper wire. Connect one end to hole A11 (same row as the LED's shorter/negative leg) and the other end to the negative (-) power rail.
steps.visual_cue: Black wire goes from row 11 to the blue (-) rail.
common_errors: Connected to positive rail instead of negative

steps.instruction: Connect the battery holder. Attach the red wire from the battery holder to the positive (+) power rail and the black wire to the negative (-) power rail.
steps.visual_cue: Battery holder wires connect to the power rails on the side of the breadboard.

steps.instruction: Insert the 3V coin battery into the holder with the positive (+) side facing up. The LED should light up!
steps.visual_cue: The LED glows. If it doesn't, check all connections and LED orientation.
common_errors: Loose connections somewhere in the circuit
